title: Wooden Joe, the loudest trumpet
summary: Wooden Joe was so loud he got his name; Kid Clayton also played Little Woods.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Can you tell us anything about Wooden Joe in the old days? I heard Wooden Joe from about 1943 on.
Wooden Joe is one of the powerful trumpet players you had here.
He was very powerful even when I heard him in the last stage.

He was one of the powerful that you had here. You'd be in a parade, you could hear him, if you didn't hear nothing else, you'd hear him. That's where he got that name, Wooden Joe. I mean, he was powerful. Wooden Joe. I never heard nobody blow louder than him yet. I mean, real, the facts. He was the loudest you ever heard. That's right.
He was about the loudest I ever heard.

He stood up to that name too. They'd say Wooden Joe. That's where he got that name, from Wooden Joe. And he played with you out at the Lake of Middleburg. That's the last one worked with him at the... Littlewoods. Littlewoods. Littlewoods. Littlewoods. That's the last one worked at me, Littlewoods. Littlewoods.
I remember a few years ago, Kid Clayton was out there in Littlewoods and a couple of other places.
